clue.text: Son who's'mediocre put on track

parts.note: something mediocre is of poor quality

explanation.surface: A father complains that his unremarkable son has been sent down a particular path in life.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoor is the trail or scent left by an animal, which a hunter follows.

clue.text: Law for traders requiring some give and take?

parts.note: to give goods is to supply them
taken as written
to take, as in 'this job takes patience', is to demand or require

explanation.surface: A rule of commerce that depends on a little compromise between the parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give and take' looks like the idiom for compromise, but read word by word it gives the two halves of the market law.
explanation.definitionFit: The economic principle that prices settle where the amount offered meets the amount wanted is the basic law of the marketplace.

clue.text: Tanker engine with top removed

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of the word is its first letter, which is taken away

parts.note: a boiler is the steam-raising part of a steam engine, standing for the engine itself

explanation.surface: A tanker whose engine has had its upper part stripped off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with top removed' drops the first letter B from BOILER.
explanation.definitionFit: An oiler is a ship that carries fuel oil, a kind of tanker.

clue.text: Leave nothing undisturbed in one of the British Isles

definitions.meaning: to rock everything, shaking up all there is
a tiny uninhabited rocky islet in the North Atlantic, claimed by the UK

explanation.surface: A search party vows to turn over every stone on a remote island.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the answer is an instruction to shake every last thing. Rockall is the lone rock far west of the Outer Hebrides, familiar from the BBC shipping forecast.
explanation.definitionFit: The islet is counted among the outlying British Isles, and the phrase splits into a command to shake everything.

clue.text: One on island returned a catalogue that's left

indicators.note: returned means the pair of pieces before it is read backwards
on means the first piece sits right up against the second

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
Cos (or Kos) is a Greek island in the Dodecanese
a catalogue is a list

explanation.surface: Someone on an island sends back a brochure that has been left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns the first pair into SOCI. 'Left' is not 'remaining' but the political wing.
explanation.definitionFit: The political left is the side of collectivists and those favouring public ownership.

clue.text: In addition, love unarmed combat

parts.note: a sum is an addition of figures
love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O

explanation.surface: Besides affection, a person enjoys fighting without weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In addition' reads as the phrase meaning 'also', but 'addition' alone is the SUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumo is Japanese wrestling, a form of fighting with bare bodies and no weapons.

clue.text: Calves, once poorly, going to recover

indicators.note: poorly suggests the letters are in bad shape and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Young cattle that were once sick are now on the road to health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poorly' rearranges CALVESONCE into the answer; 'going to' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To convalesce is to regain health gradually after an illness.

clue.text: War-god's succeeded, having brought in divine skill

indicators.note: having brought in means the second piece is taken inside the first

parts.note: Ares is the Greek god of war; the 's stands for 'has'
a divine is a clergyman, often holding a DD, Doctor of Divinity
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: The god of war has triumphed by enlisting heavenly talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'War-god's' means the war-god has, so 's is a link rather than a possessive; a divine often holds the degree Doctor of Divinity.
explanation.definitionFit: Address can mean dexterity or adroitness, as in handling a tricky matter with address.

clue.text: Confine it -doctor!

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered

explanation.surface: A patient tells the physician to keep a contagious illness under control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' rearranges CONFINEIT; the whole clue also describes what a doctor would do with something catching.
explanation.definitionFit: A contagious disease is exactly what one urges a physician to contain.

clue.text: Wonderful example of hairy old electronic components

definitions.meaning: an informal phrase for something excellent or the best

definitions.text: example of hairy old electronic components
definitions.meaning: a cat's whisker was the fine wire touching the crystal in early radio sets, and a cat has many

explanation.surface: Praise for a charmingly furry set of vintage radio parts.
explanation.walkthrough: Crystal radio sets used a thin wire called a cat's whisker; a set of those, or a feline's actual whiskers, are 'hairy'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means superlative, and literally names the hairs on a feline face that gave the old radio wire its nickname.

clue.text: I compel a crook to come to station at last?

definitions.text: I compel a crook to come to station at last?

indicators.note: crook as a verb means to bend, so these letters are bent into a new order
at last picks out the final letter of station

explanation.surface: An officer forcing a criminal to report to the station at long last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crook' rearranges ICOMPELA; 'at last' adds the N ending 'station'. The whole clue is something an officer might say.
explanation.definitionFit: A constable is the one who makes a criminal come to the station.

clue.text: Author in debt (not half) to rival

indicators.note: not half means only the first half of debt is kept

parts.note: a rival is a foe or opponent

explanation.surface: A writer, owing money, turns to a competitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' keeps DE from DEBT.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Defoe was the English writer of Robinson Crusoe.

clue.text: Grubby collaborationist imprisoning Resistance

indicators.note: imprisoning means the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: Pierre Laval was the Vichy French premier who collaborated with Nazi Germany
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A dirty wartime traitor locks up members of the French Resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grubby' is not 'dirty' but 'like a grub'.
explanation.definitionFit: A grub is an insect in its early stage, so grubby here means in that stage of life.

clue.text: Farewell to north — spies southern port

parts.note: vale is Latin for farewell
the CIA is the American intelligence agency, a body of spies

explanation.surface: Bidding goodbye to the north, secret agents head for a harbour in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' joins the first two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Valencia is a Spanish seaport on the Mediterranean, in southern Europe.

clue.text: It can provide accompaniment to a number I knocked out

indicators.note: knocked out suggests the letters are battered into a new shape

explanation.surface: A percussion instrument plays along while a singer belts out a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked out' rearranges TOANUMBERI. The fodder starts with 'to', which reads as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The small hand drum with jingles is shaken to keep rhythm behind a song.

clue.text: Nurse, they say, needs some soap and sponge

parts.note: nurses are popularly called angels
a cake is a block of soap

explanation.surface: A nurse needs a bit of soap and a sponge for a bed bath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sponge' looks like the bathroom item but is the light cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Angel cake is a very light, airy type of sponge made with egg whites.

clue.text: Girl, extremely loving and alluring

indicators.note: extremely takes only the extreme, or outermost, letters of girl

parts.note: amorous means loving or full of romantic desire

explanation.surface: A young woman who is very affectionate and attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' looks like an intensifier for 'loving' but takes the first and last letters of 'Girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamorous means having an attractive, exciting charm.

clue.text: Move through water briefly beside ship-one unlikely to be in Navy?

definitions.text: one unlikely to be in Navy

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: to swim is to move through water
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Someone swims for a short while beside a ship, though they would never join the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts SWIM to SWI. Switzerland is landlocked, so a Swiss person would hardly be a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Switzerland, a country with no coastline, is not likely to serve at sea.

clue.text: Pull to one side, in a manner of speaking

parts.note: to draw is to pull
L, for left, is one side

explanation.surface: Someone draws a person aside, or so the saying goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a manner of speaking' looks like the idiom 'so to speak', but the definition is the literal phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawl is a slow way of talking with drawn-out vowels.

clue.text: Advance with difficulty round one river or another

parts.note: to limp is to move forward with difficulty
a round shape is the letter O
the Po is the great river of northern Italy

explanation.surface: Struggling forward around one river or the next.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one river or another' reads as a vague phrase, but the Po is one river and the answer another.
explanation.definitionFit: The Limpopo is a southern African river, so it is a second river after the Po.

clue.text: It's not a minister's place to encourage judiciary

parts.note: to back someone is to support or encourage them
the bench is the body of judges, the judiciary

explanation.surface: A minister has no business pressuring the judges.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition looks like a constitutional statement; in Parliament it is where non-ministers sit.
explanation.definitionFit: In the House of Commons, the rear benches are where MPs without government office sit.

clue.text: Showed resentment as brother was unemployed

parts.note: idled means was out of work

explanation.surface: Someone was bitter because a sibling was out of work.
explanation.definitionFit: To bridle is to take offence, drawing back the head like a horse reined in.

clue.text: Big opera company has run with new production of 4 dn

parts.note: ENO is English National Opera
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: a new production rearranges the work, so the letters of the other entry are reordered

parts.note: the answer to 4 down, the Japanese wrestling

explanation.surface: A large opera company stages a new show about Japanese wrestling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new production of' rearranges SUMO into MOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Enormous means very large, just as sumo wrestlers are.

clue.text: Shed light on problem rejected for test paper

parts.note: lit means illuminated, shed light on

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: Clarifying an issue that has been dismissed from an exam paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns SUM into MUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Litmus is the dye used on strips that change colour to show acidity, a chemical indicator paper.

clue.text: Son wearing fur in cold city

indicators.note: wearing means the second piece is clothed in the first

parts.note: mink is a valuable fur

explanation.surface: A boy in a fur coat in a freezing town.
explanation.definitionFit: Minsk, capital of Belarus, has bitter winters.

clue.text: Goodness gets one's vote of approval

parts.note: one is I, and the 's adds an S
aye or ay is the vote in favour

explanation.surface: Good conduct earns someone a vote in their favour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goodness' looks like virtue but is the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild British exclamations of surprise.

clue.text: Eager to have oxygen in plentiful supply

parts.note: agog means eager or excited
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Someone anxious to have lots of oxygen to breathe.
explanation.definitionFit: A-gogo means in abundance, as in 'wine a-gogo'.

clue.text: It's enclosed in part of shoe for freshness

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held: 'It's enclosed in part of shoe for freshness' (INSOLENCE). INSOLE is part of a shoe, but no reading of 'It's enclosed' gives the remaining NCE, and a search of the exact text found no parse.
annotationWithheld.clue: It's enclosed in part of shoe for freshness

clue.text: Finding musical entertainment jolly

parts.note: a disco is a dance with recorded music
jolly is British informal for very, as in 'jolly good'

explanation.surface: Turning up a cheerful show with music.
explanation.definitionFit: A discovery is something found, a find.

clue.text: Almost one of the top rank as composer

indicators.note: almost means the word stops one letter short of the end

parts.note: a duke is of the highest rank of the peerage

explanation.surface: Nearly an aristocrat of the highest order as a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts DUKE to DUK.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Dukas was the French composer of The Sorcerer's Apprentice.
